author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Alexander Zverev reached the U.S. Open semifinals Thursday by defeating Botic van de Zandschulp 6-2, 7-5, 6-1 at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Zverev overcame five early double faults and broke in the fifth game of the opening set. Van de Zandschulp threatened to level the match in the second, but the German won three straight games late in the set and carried the momentum into a one-sided third.

The victory sends Zverev into a semifinal against Karen Khachanov, a rematch of their gold-medal match at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. Zverev, the 2020 U.S. Open runner-up and reigning French Open champion, has now reached the semifinals at all four majors this season.

His 23 Grand Slam match wins in 2026 also surpassed Boris Becker’s 1989 record of 22 for a German man in one year, according to Reuters. Zverev is the only player remaining in the men’s draw who has already won a major title, but he still needs two victories in New York to add a second Grand Slam championship.
dek: The German defeated Botic van de Zandschulp 6-2, 7-5, 6-1 and will face Karen Khachanov for a place in the final.
headline: Alexander Zverev reaches U.S. Open semifinals in straight sets
